sources.note: HandleProcessExit: records lifecycle.KindProcessExited and deletes the row, whatever state the row was in. #1800 added a retain branch in front of it and #1860 removed it again — the daemon is not the agent's parent, so no exit status is available on any platform and a crash cannot be told from a deliberate quit.
SweepDeadPIDs: 5s base interval backing off to 15s after 3 clean sweeps; the probe is syscall.Kill(pid, 0). This is the safety net behind the instant kqueue/pidfd exit edge.
step_sigkill kills by pgrep -f 'claude.*--session-id $UUID'; sigkill is declared in DRIVE_ELICITS so recipe-lint accepts the step.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

No mock is needed: the driver's `sigkill` step kills the active session's claude PID by `pgrep -f "claude.*--session-id $UUID"`. The recipe kills mid-turn — after the prompt lands, before `wait_turn` — so the transcript freezes with the turn still open.

The daemon observable is the PID exit itself: `process_exited` on the kqueue/pidfd edge (or within one liveness sweep), followed by the row's deletion. There is no verdict to derive, and that is the point of the cell — #1800 tried to derive one from the session's shape and #1860 removed it, because irrlicht is not the agent's parent and gets no exit status, so a segfault, an OOM kill and a clean `exit(0)` are one observation. The guess was wrong for the two commonest endings (an ESC interrupt and a denied tool prompt), and a wrong red is worse than no red.

## Shares its outcome with 1.2 session-end, and is kept anyway

1.2 also SIGKILLs and its sessions also disappear. This cell is kept separate because it is the only one that kills mid-turn under a BOUND PID with the turn still open — the exact shape the removed inference keyed on — so it is where a re-introduced guess would show up first. The prompt is deliberately long-running so the kill lands inside the turn rather than after it.

## Recordings predate #1860

Both committed recordings were captured on daemons carrying #1800, so their frozen events.jsonl holds a `working→error` and no `process_exited` at all. The cell is `known_failing` until it is re-recorded; see expected.jsonl's notes.
